source.title: Descriptions of Cantor Sets: A Set-Theoretic Survey and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Find an explicit set-theoretic formula or a recursive set-theoretic formula for deterministic Cantor subsets of [0,1] that are generated by an iterated-function system with K ≥ 2 maps and that do not preserve bilateral symmetry.

evidence.quote: The preceding survey has shown that three natural families of deterministic Cantor sets—two of measure zero with explicit descriptions and one of non–negative measure defined recursively—share a common symmetric architecture and possess rational construction end-points; indeed, the classical middle-third Cantor set lies in the intersection of all three.

(OP1) Asymmetric constructions. Devise explicit or recursive set-theoretic formulas for Cantor sets generated by iterated-function systems (IFS) with K ≥ 2 maps that do not preserve bilateral symmetry.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether one can obtain descriptive set-theoretic formulas for deterministic Cantor sets whose retained intervals have irrational end-points, while still allowing an iterated-function-system construction with K ≥ 2 components.

evidence.quote: The preceding survey has shown that three natural families of deterministic Cantor sets—two of measure zero with explicit descriptions and one of non–negative measure defined recursively—share a common symmetric architecture and possess rational construction end-points; indeed, the classical middle-third Cantor set lies in the intersection of all three.
(OP2) Irrational end-points. Find descriptive formulas when the retained intervals have irrational end-points, again allowing K ≥ 2 IFS components.
